Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the HIPAA / BAA discussion we had with the HealthCloud team:

- Questions raised: BAA availability, acceptable deployment modes for PHI, SOC 2 status, and next steps for our vendor security questionnaire.

What I can confirm now: 
- Redwood can execute a BAA under standard enterprise agreements. We typically require customers with PHI workloads to run on Dedicated or Private deployments for stronger isolation and customer-controlled networking. Hosted API can be considered on a case-by-case basis for limited PHI scenarios — we'll need to validate retention/configuration constraints.
- We have a SOC 2 Type II report available for review and a DPA for GDPR needs.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I’ve attached a short security questionnaire (HealthCloud_Security_Questionnaire.pdf) — could you share the completed version or tell me if you prefer we fill anything on your side?

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the clear summary. I’m the infra lead on PHI enablement at Redwood; wanted to address the deployment and PHI boundary questions you raised. TL;DR: Dedicated and Private are the recommended/eligible modes for PHI production workloads; Hosted can be considered for limited-scope, short-retention workflows but requires additional configuration and legal approval. 

Details: 
- BAA: Redwood can sign a BAA. For production PHI we require either Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools with tenant isolation and optional VPC peering) or Private (customer-managed control plane / on-prem) deployments. These provide stronger isolation, customer KMS/HSM integration, and network controls.
- Hosted API: We do not generally approve long-term PHI use on our multi-tenant hosted endpoints. Exceptions may be made for short-term, non-persistent ingestion where customers encrypt and manage keys and agree to strict retention and logging policies — we’ll need security review and a contractual addendum.
- PHI boundaries: Redwood’s runtime supports prefix/KV caching controls and token-level redaction. For PHI flows we recommend disabling long-term KV caching, enforcing request-level skipping of logs for PHI fields, and using customer-managed KMS for any keys.
- SOC 2 & compliance artifacts: We have a current SOC 2 Type II report available for review and a DPA for GDPR. I’ll share the SOC 2 summary and control mappings on the drive link Marissa included.

Attachments I’m sharing here: Redwood_Draft_BAA_2026.docx (draft BAA for redline) and HealthCloud_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (filled template with technical answers).

Proposed next steps:
1) HealthCloud to complete the questionnaire items that require business context (data flows, retention windows).
2) Schedule a 30-min technical review with our infra/security engineers (I can do 11:00am PT tomorrow).
3) Legal teams to review the draft BAA in parallel — we can accept redlines in DocuSign.

If you want, I can also prepare a short one-page architecture diagram showing where PHI is in scope.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
